The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Milan Raj R in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner' case are as under:
2.

That on 31.01.2021 at about 00.30 a.m. deceased Milan Raj R. was traveling along with his friends as one of the occupant in a Car bearing registration No.KA-04-MV-4581 with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, infront of Raga Apartment, Kannuru-Belahalli Main Road, Bangalore City, at that time, driver of Concrete Mixer lorry bearing registration No.KA-01-AK-8626 drove the same in a negligent manner, and suddenly took turn without observing the vehicle coming from behind and without taking any precautions and giving any indications.

Due to which,
deceased succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted at Dr.Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital and the dead body was handed over to the petitioner.

Subsequently, the petitioner has spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other Radha vs Chandra Shekar K.H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111268787/
2 incidental expenses.
3.

It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
aged about 19 years, working as a student cum real estates and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioner become dark, miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing registration No.KA-04-MV-4581 and Concrete Mixer lorry bearing registration No.KA-01- AK-8626.
In this regard, Chikkajala Police have registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle in Crime No.17/2021.
As such, the respondents No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 to 4 have appeared through their respective counsel, the respondent No.1 to 4 have filed their written statement respectively.
6. The respondent No.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent is the RC owner of the Volkswagen Polo car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and the said vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 and the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
Further, denied about the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626.
Hence respondent No.3 and 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further, this respondent has issued third party cover policy in favour of first respondent in respect of Car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581.
Under the said cover the risk of the occupants travelling in the car is not covered.
Further stated that, the driver of car was driving the car under the influence of intoxicating alcohol violating the provisions of M.V. Act.
Further the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA- 01-AK-8626.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
8. The respondent No.3 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent is the RC owner of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 and the said vehicle has been duly insured with the respondent No.4.

Further, denied about the age,
avocation and income of the deceased.

The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving Radha vs Chandra Shekar K.H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111268787/
3 of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.

With all these main grounds,
prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
9. In the written statement, the respondent No.4 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further, this respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Concrete Mixer lorry and liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581, who drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, without driving licence, without wearing seat belt and also under influence of Alcohol and himself dashed to the concrete mixer lorry bearing registration No. KA-01-AK-8628.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

10. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, her son Milan Raj R S/o Late S.K. Raju was died in the road traffic accident which occurred on 31.01.2021 at about 00.30 a.m., in front of Raga Apartment, Kannuru-Belahalli Main Road, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the Car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and Concrete Mixer lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626?
2) Whether the petitioner prove that, she is the legal heir of deceased Milan Raj R.?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4) What order or award?

11. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
12.

On the other hand, respondent No.4 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and the respondent No.1 examined himself as RW2 and got marked document as Ex.R1 and respondent No.2 examined its Area Manager Legal as RW3 and got marked document as Ex.R2.
13. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

14. My findings to the above issues as follows:

4
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: In the Affirmative Issue No.3: Partly in Affirmative Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
15.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-04-MV- 4581 and the driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently Milan Raj R. died at the spot.

16. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 have contended in their written statements that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 and not on the part of the driver of the car.

17. Further the respondent No.3 & 4 being the owner and insurer of the concrete mixer lorry bearing registration No.KA-01-AK-8626 have contended in their written statements that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
Hence, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the concrete mixer lorry.

18. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, the petitioner have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against both the vehicles in question.
On the other hand, onus shifts on the respondents to prove the same by means of cogent and convincing evidence.
19. In order to prove her case, the petitioner examined herself as PW1.
In her examination-in- chief by way of affidavit, she has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P10.
Ex. P1

-true copy of the FIR, Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P4-true copy of spot mahazar,
Ex.P5- true copy of IMV report, Ex.P6 & Ex.P8-true copies of notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex.P7 &
Ex.P9-true copies of reply to notice u/s 133 of MV Act.
Ex.P10-true copy of inquest, Ex.P11-true copy of P.M. report and Ex.P11-true copy of charge sheet.

20. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Channegowda, son of the deceased, the S.H.O. of Chickjala Traffic Police have registered the case against the drivers of both the vehicles for the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet alleging that the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 have committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
21.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.4 has examined its Legal Manager- Legal as RW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.

Radha vs Chandra Shekar K.H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111268787/
5 22.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 being the owner examined himself as RW2.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.

He has placed Ex.R1.
23.
Further respondent No.2 has examined its area Manager Legal as RW3.
He has placed Ex.R2.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
24. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, nothing has been elicited from her mouth to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.
Even at the time of evidence of RW1 to RW3 no reliable documents placed before this court to disprove the case of the petitioner.
25. Added to this, on perusal of the recitals of the police documents, there is clear narration about the involvement of both the vehicles in the accident.
On keen observation of the evidence of PW1 and the documents produced by the petitioner, it is clear that due to the negligence of both the drivers of the offending vehicles the accident occurred.

26. Apart from this, there is no doubt that, the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer clearly reveals that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and the driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing registration No.KA-01-AK-8626.
On perusal of the evidence and the materials placed by the petitioner, it is clear that the charge sheet is not the conclusive proof.
At the most, that may be a circumstance which has to be considered along with other materials on record.

To disprove the charge sheet contents, no supportive evidence is available on record to impeach the recitals of Ex.P12.
27.

In the light of the evidence placed by PW1 and the documents before this court, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and the driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing registration No.KA-01-AK-8626.

In the said accident,
Milan Raj R. succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2 & 3:
28.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioner are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioner is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioner, to prove the relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P13 to Ex.P14 i.e., aadhar card of deceased and the petitioner have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioner and the deceased.

29. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioner, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioner is the mother, in her middle age, lost her son, as well as the care of her son, who was the backbone of the family.

The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic Radha vs Chandra Shekar K.H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111268787/
6 status of the petitioner.
By taking into consideration of all these factors along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioner is the dependent to the deceased during his lifetime.
30. The petitioner herein, has placed SSLC Marks card, which is marked at Ex.P15 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 8.6.2002.
The accident occurred on 31.01.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 19 years.

For his age, multiplier '18' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
31.

In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was a student and during his free hours he was doing real estate business and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
There is no iota of document to show that deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Hence, it is apt to be considered notional income.

32. Another point to be taken in to consideration herein that, as per the petition, the deceased was a bachelor, for deduction of the personal and living expenses, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.
33. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income,
an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
34. Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor, deduction towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 19 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "18" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the petitioner herein Radha vs Chandra Shekar K.H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111268787/
7 as on the date of the accident, was not having permanent job.

As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
And Rs.1,80,000/- per year.

Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased,
comes to (Rs.1,80,000+72,000)= Rs.2,52,000/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus net loss income comes to Rs.1,26,000/-
(Rs.2,52,000- Rs.1,26,000).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "18".

In toto it comes to Rs.22,68,000/- .
35.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

36. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of consortium.

sentences.text: 37. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.

Compensation heads Compensation  Amount  Towards loss of Rs.22,68,000-00  dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 44,000-00  consortium  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & Rs. 16,500-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Total Rs.23,45,000-00 Radha vs Chandra Shekar K.H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111268787/
8 38.

Accordingly, the petitioner herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.23,45,000/-
(Rupees twenty three lakhs forty five thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.
103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020 from the date of petition till its realisation.

LIABILITY:-
39.

As regards the liability is concerned, as already discussed in issue No.1 that, the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 and driver of the concrete mixer lorry bearing No.KA- 01-AK-8626.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
40. Further as per Ex.R2 insurance policy of the car bearing No.KA-04-MV-4581 was valid from 12.10.2018 to 11.10.2021.
As per records the insurance policy of Lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-8626 was valid from 15.5.2020 to 14.5.2021.
The alleged accident had taken place on 31.1.2021.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy of the car and concrete mixer lorry, the respondent No.2 & 4 are liable to pay the compensation at the ratio of 50% each with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition,
till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Affirmative Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
41.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,45,000/-
(Rupees twenty three lakhs forty five thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 & 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner at the ratio of 50% each with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, 40% of her share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining Radha vs Chandra Shekar K.H on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111268787/
9
60% of her share shall be released to her through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
[ Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 4th day of December 2025).
